as.bilingual_pair_policy: This Ghana Mathematics curriculum is English-only. Do not create bilingual pairs, translations, or cross-language duplicate candidates. Preserve visible English source text exactly. If non-English text appears incidentally, keep it only as source-visible text and do not translate it or pair it with an English candidate unless the document itself explicitly presents both versions as equivalent official curriculum text.

as.sfi_dedup_instructions:
Deduplicate Ghana Mathematics Basic 4–6 SFI candidates conservatively. Merge candidates only when they represent the same source-visible curriculum item. Same statement_type plus same normalized official code is strong merge evidence only when the descriptions/source_text are compatible and the source references are the same item, adjacent table-window overlap, or a clear continuation duplicate. Do not treat Ghana official codes as globally unique identity keys: the source contains apparent code reuse, duplication, and numbering anomalies where the same Content Standard or Indicator code is attached to different mathematical statements. Same official code with materially different descriptions, different source rows/segments, or different mathematical content should not be merged. When the bounded evidence shows they are distinct source-visible curriculum items, keep them separate as individual SFIs and preserve same-code/different-content audit evidence for manual review and disambiguated final IDs. Use conflict or needs_review for same-code candidates only when they appear to be competing or incompatible extractions of the same source-visible item, or when the bounded evidence is insufficient to decide whether they are distinct source items. Similar or identical text with different official codes usually represents distinct Ghana curriculum items and should be keep_separate unless the bounded evidence clearly shows duplicate extraction of the same source item. Treat malformed visible codes with spaces, punctuation, or OCR/source numbering issues cautiously: merge only when the intended official code and source item are clear; otherwise choose needs_review. For no-code Grade, Strand, and Sub-Strand groupings, do not merge by label alone. BASIC 4, BASIC 5, and BASIC 6 are grade-scoped organizers; merge case/format variants of the same grade when statement_type=Grade and there is no direct visible evidence that they refer to different grade scopes, but keep different grades separate. Inherited source_context_labels alone should not block same-grade merges because they may be stale or noisy around divider pages, repeated heading blocks, or layout transitions. Strand and Sub-Strand labels such as Number Operations, Fractions, Measurement, Position/Transformation, Data, or repeated local numbers like Strand 1 and Sub-Strand 1 may recur under different grades or hierarchy contexts; merge only when the label, statement_type, and visible source context indicate the same organizer, otherwise keep_separate. Source-row/header overlap, same source segment, same window proximity, duplicate buckets, and same-code buckets are review signals only, not automatic merge rules.

Known Basic 4 fractions editorial anomaly:
- In the Basic 4 Fractions section, the Content Standard coded B4.1.3.1 with description "Develop an understanding of equivalent and improper fractions" is a legitimate distinct source item. Keep this candidate separate.
- Later continuation rows incorrectly print B4.1.3.1 beside the description "Demonstrate an understanding of strategies for comparing, adding and subtracting fractions (same denominator, or one being a multiple of the others)." The same description is subsequently introduced as B4.1.3.2. Treat the B4.1.3.1 occurrence with this comparison/addition/subtraction description as an editorially mislabelled occurrence of the B4.1.3.2 Content Standard.
- When these candidates occur in the same bounded review set: (1) keep the B4.1.3.1 equivalent/improper-fractions Content Standard separate; (2) merge the comparison/addition/subtraction candidate printed as B4.1.3.1 with the candidate printed as B4.1.3.2; (3) preserve both printed codes, source_text values, row provenance, and the source anomaly in the merge evidence; (4) do not rewrite either extraction candidate or silently replace its source-visible code; and (5) do not return conflict or needs_review for this exact known pattern.
- This document-specific rule overrides the general presumption that identical descriptions with different official codes normally remain separate.
as.sfi_extraction_instructions: Extract candidate StandardsFrameworkItems (SFIs) from the Ghana Mathematics curriculum only when the visible text is an official curriculum framework item or structural organizer within the target Basic 4–6 curriculum scope. Treat BASIC 4, BASIC 5, and BASIC 6 headings as Standard Grouping SFIs. Treat Strand headings and Sub-Strand headings as Standard Grouping SFIs when they are visible as curriculum organizers. When a single visible heading line or block contains both a Strand and a Sub-Strand, extract both source-visible organizers as separate Standard Grouping SFI candidates. Treat Content Standards with official Basic 4–6 codes such as B4.1.1.1, B5.1.1.1, or B6.1.1.1 as Standard SFIs. Treat Indicators with official Basic 4–6 codes such as B4.1.1.1.1, B5.1.1.1.1, or B6.1.1.1.1 as Standard SFIs. Do not extract KG1, KG2, B1, B2, or B3 codes, labels, sample rows, or annotation examples as SFI candidates when they appear in overview, organization, scope-and-sequence, annotation, or code-explanation sections. Those earlier-grade examples are explanatory context for the code system, not target Basic 4–6 curriculum items for this run. Do not extract LearningComponents in this step: do not decompose a content standard or indicator into smaller skills, concepts, lesson objectives, or teachable subskills. Treat exemplars, examples beginning with E.g., classroom activities, assessment suggestions, teacher guidance, resources, duration/time allocations, values, and pedagogical notes as non-SFI text. Do not emit routine auxiliary candidates for this material; use an auxiliary candidate only when source-visible text is genuinely ambiguous and likely to be mistaken for an SFI. Treat Subject Specific Practices and Core Competencies as non-SFI guidance and do not emit routine auxiliary candidates for them unless a document-specific profile explicitly overrides this policy. Repeated table headers and repeated continuation labels are not SFIs. Preserve source-language wording. The description must preserve the complete official Grade, Strand, Sub-Strand, Content Standard, or Indicator wording. For visible organizers, retain the hierarchy label, ordinal, punctuation, and topic together; for example, preserve "Sub-Strand 3: Variables and Equations" rather than shortening it to "Variables and Equations". Do not include a separately printed item code in description. Keep the formatting-normalized code in statement_code and preserve the exact raw code surface in the source_text evidence quote. A complete four- or five-component Basic 4–6 code that is printed immediately adjacent to statement text, or that differs only by spacing around periods or trailing punctuation, is formatting-recoverable and should be separated from the statement without changing any code character or numeric component. Thus "B5. 1.2.3.1 Determine basic division fact up to 81" uses statement_code="B5.1.2.3.1", and "B5.1. 4.1.3 Round decimals to the nearest tenth and hundredth" uses statement_code="B5.1.4.1.3", while source_text preserves each raw printed form. Use statement_code only when an official complete code is visible in the candidate's own source text. Preserve visibly malformed or incomplete source codes in source_text and keep statement_code null rather than repairing a prefix, adding a component, or changing a numeric component. Within one extraction result, identical repeated continuation occurrences of the same statement type, normalized code, and complete description must produce one candidate with all contributing row indexes; the same code with materially different descriptions must remain separate.
as.sfi_extraction_validation_instructions:
Validate Ghana Mathematics Basic 4-6 SFI extraction conservatively and source-faithfully. Apply the following curriculum-specific rules in addition to the generic checker rules and the extraction instructions.

1. Target scope and non-target sections
- The target SFIs are the official Basic 4, Basic 5, and Basic 6 hierarchy and statements in the detailed standards section: visible Grade, Strand, and Sub-Strand organizers; coded Content Standards; and coded or clearly source-designated Indicators.
- Reject SFI candidates drawn from the cover, publication details, foreword, table of contents, rationale, philosophy, general or subject aims, instructional expectations, core competencies, learning domains, skills and processes, attitudes, values, assessment, time allocation, pedagogy, inclusion, differentiation, ICT guidance, panel-member lists, and other front or back matter.
- Reject organizer names and codes that appear only in the annotation, organization, structure, or scope-and-sequence explanations. The KG1, KG2, B1, B2, and B3 examples in the curriculum-reference diagram and sample table are explanatory examples, not target SFIs. Likewise, B4-B6 strand and sub-strand names in overview or scope-and-sequence tables summarize coverage and must not be extracted from those summary tables.
- Do not interpret the cover phrase "BASIC 4 - 6", a table-of-contents entry, a progression statement such as "B1 to B6", or a B4/B5/B6 column label as a Grade SFI. A Grade candidate requires a visible grade organizer in the detailed curriculum section, such as "BASIC 4", "BASIC 5", or "BASIC 6".

2. Grade, Strand, and Sub-Strand organizers
- Accept a visible BASIC 4, BASIC 5, or BASIC 6 heading as a Grade SFI. Accept visible Strand and Sub-Strand headings in the detailed standards section as Standard Grouping SFIs.
- When a visible heading area contains Grade, Strand, and/or Sub-Strand labels together, return each organizer as a separate candidate in source order. Do not combine "Basic 4 / Strand 1 / Sub-strand 1" into one candidate.
- Preserve the complete visible organizer label as the description, including the hierarchy term, ordinal, punctuation, and topic. For example, "Sub-Strand 3: Variables and Equations" must remain exactly that full description; shortening it to "Variables and Equations" is a material error. Do not reduce a Strand or Sub-Strand candidate to only its ordinal, and do not create a candidate from the generic words "STRAND", "SUB-STRAND", "CONTENT STANDARD", or other table-column headers.
- Do not infer a missing organizer from a coded statement, a section path, a scope-and-sequence table, or expected hierarchy. The source contains missing, repeated, and inconsistent Sub-Strand headings and ordinals. Extract only organizers that are visible in the current raw block or table content.
- Treat repeated organizer names as source-scoped. The same Strand or Sub-Strand label can recur under different grades, and different visible Sub-Strand labels can share the same ordinal. Do not delete or rewrite a visible organizer merely because its ordinal or wording conflicts with another part of the document.

3. Content Standards and Indicators
- A normal Ghana Content Standard is the official statement in the left CONTENT STANDARD(S) column, usually paired with a four-component B4/B5/B6 code such as B4.1.1.1. A normal Indicator is the official learning-outcome statement in the INDICATORS AND EXEMPLARS column, usually paired with a five-component code such as B4.1.1.1.1.
- Use source role, placement, and statement formatting together with the code. Do not classify every imperative sentence as an Indicator: exemplar activities are also imperative. Conversely, do not reject a concise imperative such as "Determine...", "Represent...", "Identify...", or "Create..." when it is the bold official coded indicator statement.
- A single table cell or row can contain more than one Content Standard and/or more than one Indicator. Split each separately bounded official code-and-statement pair into its own candidate. Do not combine neighboring standards because they share a row, cell, page, or source window.
- One official statement can wrap across lines or continue across adjacent raw rows. Preserve the complete statement as one candidate when the visible fragments clearly belong to the same code and statement. Do not split a statement at a line break, page break, mathematical expression, or column wrap.
- Do not truncate an Indicator at the first sentence when the bold official statement continues across lines. Do not append its E.g., Note, NB, Key Concept, diagram explanation, or teaching directions to the Indicator description.

4. Continuation pages and repeated material
- "CONT'D", "CONT’D", and equivalent continuation markers are page-layout labels, not part of an SFI description and not separate candidates.
- Repeated table headers and repeated column labels are not SFIs.
- A continued left-column Content Standard may be repeated across several pages or rows while new Indicators appear beside it. The repeated code and description still identify the same Content Standard. Within one validation result, group by canonical statement type, normalized code, and complete normalized description. Identical repeated occurrences must produce one source-grounded candidate with all contributing raw row/header indexes. Emitting separate candidates for those identical occurrences is a material error. Duplicate occurrences in different extraction windows may remain for downstream deduplication.
- A continuation row that contains only E.g. material, notes, diagrams, calculations, or activities does not create a new Indicator. Extract a new Indicator only when a new official indicator statement is visible. If the continued Content Standard is visible, it may still support the Content Standard candidate.
- If the same visible code is attached to materially different official descriptions, those are not continuation duplicates. Keep the distinct source statements as separate candidates and let later deduplication preserve the same-code/different-content evidence.

5. Material that is not an SFI
- Exclude all exemplars and example sequences beginning with "E.g.", including classroom tasks, worked examples, questions for learners, games, investigations, sample calculations, number charts, diagrams, illustrations, manipulatives, worksheets, and suggested teaching procedures.
- Exclude "Learners develop:" and all Subject Specific Practices and Core Competencies, including Problem Solving Skills, Critical Thinking, Justification of Ideas, Collaborative Learning, Attention to Precision, Cultural Identity, Global Citizenship, Personal Development and Leadership, and similar lists.
- Exclude Note, NB, Key Concept, reminders, cautions, cross-references, figure captions used as teaching guidance, and statements such as "Diagram is on the next page".
- Exclude mathematical facts, formulas, tables, chart labels, sample data, and image/figure descriptions unless the exact text is part of the official bold Content Standard or Indicator statement itself.
- A code mentioned inside an exemplar, note, cross-reference, diagram, or explanatory paragraph does not establish a new candidate. The code must visibly introduce the official source item in the appropriate source role.
- Do not create LearningComponents from the concepts, subskills, methods, examples, or activities contained inside a Content Standard or Indicator.

6. Ghana code anomalies and malformed source text
- Preserve genuine source anomalies; do not silently rewrite a code to make the hierarchy look regular. Use statement_code only when an exact valid code is visibly supported by the candidate's own source text and matches the configured code type.
- Spaces around periods, inconsistent spacing, and adjacent trailing punctuation can occur in otherwise clear codes. Use the deterministic code match's normalized value in statement_code and preserve its raw value in source_text; do not change any alphanumeric component. For example, "B5. 1.2.3.1 Determine basic division fact up to 81" requires statement_code="B5.1.2.3.1", and "B5.1. 4.1.3 Round decimals to the nearest tenth and hundredth" requires statement_code="B5.1.4.1.3". Leaving either code null is a material validation error.
- The Basic 4 Number Operations page visibly prints an extra leading "B" before "B4.1.2.1.1". Treat B4.1.2.1.1 as the intended Indicator code when that exact five-component code is visible, but do not include the stray standalone "B" in statement_code or the Indicator description.
- Some source items have a clear official Indicator role but a malformed code. Do not drop the learning outcome solely because its code is malformed, and do not reclassify it as a Content Standard solely from component count. When the role and official statement are clear but no valid exact Indicator code is visible, retain the Indicator candidate with statement_code=null and preserve the visible anomalous prefix in source_text when needed for evidence.
- In particular, the questionnaire statement printed as "B6.5.2.2 Design and administer a questionnaire..." appears in the Indicators and Exemplars column beside Content Standard B6.4.1.2. Treat the learning-outcome statement as an Indicator, but do not invent a fifth component or silently rewrite the visible code; use statement_code=null unless a valid exact indicator code is visible in the same source item.
- The probability statement printed as "P6.4.2.2.3 Explain that the experimental probability approaches..." is an official Indicator statement with a visibly anomalous P prefix. Do not change P to B. Extract the Indicator with statement_code=null unless an exact valid B-code is independently visible for that same statement.
- Glued forms such as a complete five-component code immediately followed by statement text must be separated when the full code is visibly recoverable from the candidate's own raw source. For example, "B5.2.3.1.3Create a problem for a given equation" must produce statement_code="B5.2.3.1.3", description="Create a problem for a given equation", and source_text preserving the complete visible code-and-statement text. Treat a null statement_code in this formatting-only case as a material validation error. Do not borrow a code from a neighboring statement, infer a missing digit, change a prefix, or repair an incorrect numeric component.
- Do not invent candidates for missing sequence numbers, and do not assume that Indicator or Content Standard numbering is complete or sequential.

7. Known same-code/different-content cases and editorial artifacts
- Do not treat an official code as globally unique identity during extraction validation. The source reuses some codes for different official statements.
- B4.1.3.1 is visibly attached to two different Content Standards: "Develop an understanding of equivalent and improper fractions" and "Demonstrate an understanding of strategies for comparing, adding and subtracting fractions (same denominator, or one being a multiple of the others)". Both are separate Content Standard candidates when visible. Do not merge them or choose one as the correction of the other.
- The red struck-through "12 x 12" printed beneath both B4.1.3.1 statements is deleted editorial residue and is not part of either Content Standard description or source evidence quote.
- B6.3.3.5 is visibly reused for both "Describe the position of objects in space using the cardinal points" and "Perform a single transformation (i.e. reflection translation) on a 2D shape". B6.3.3.5.1 is likewise reused for two different Indicators. Preserve each distinct source-visible statement as a separate candidate; do not combine them because the codes match.
- More generally, when identical codes have materially different descriptions or different source locations, preserve each visible official statement separately. Same code is not a reason to delete, merge, paraphrase, or force descriptions to agree.
- Ignore obvious deleted/struck-through editorial text and obvious neighboring-cell spillover that is not part of the official bold statement. Do not otherwise repair grammar, spelling, punctuation, mathematical notation, or source wording.

8. Description, source text, language, and citations
- description must contain the complete official source-visible wording of the Grade/Strand/Sub-Strand label, Content Standard, or Indicator. Remove only a separately represented item code; preserve organizer hierarchy terms, ordinals, punctuation, and separators. Do not include the table column header, CONT'D marker, examples, competencies, notes, or unrelated neighboring text unless that text is actually part of the official statement wording. Including the candidate's code at the beginning or end of description, or shortening a complete visible organizer label, is a material validation error that requires a corrected result.
- When statement_code is non-null, it must equal the applicable deterministic code match's normalized value, while source_text must visibly pair the corresponding exact raw code surface with the complete candidate description. Preserve source-visible spacing and immediate adjacency between the raw code and statement text. Do not use a code appearing elsewhere in the window.
- For a clearly official no-code candidate caused by a malformed source code, source_text may include the malformed visible prefix plus the complete official statement, while statement_code remains null.
- Preserve Ghanaian English wording, capitalization, spelling, grammar, punctuation, symbols, ranges, units, and mathematical notation as visible. Do not improve or modernize the wording and do not translate.
- For table candidates, cite only the raw header/body row indexes that visibly contribute to the candidate. Do not cite the Subject Specific Practices/Core Competencies column or exemplar-only rows as evidence for an official statement. Include every adjacent raw row genuinely needed to reconstruct a split statement, but do not add unrelated context rows.
- Do not quote canonical headers, filldown helper values, section_path text, or inferred hierarchy as candidate evidence.

9. Validation decision
- Set passed=true only when the draft has complete coverage of all visible target SFIs in the window, contains no non-SFI material, separates distinct official statements correctly, preserves complete source wording, assigns source roles correctly, and handles codes and citations according to these rules.
- When correcting, return a complete replacement result in source order. Renumber candidates after all additions, removals, splits, or reordering. Preserve a clearly official Content Standard or Indicator even when its code is anomalous; prefer statement_code=null over inventing or silently repairing a code.
- Use auxiliary candidates only for unusually ambiguous source-visible material that is genuinely likely to be mistaken for an SFI. Treat auxiliary records for routine exemplars, competencies, notes, front matter, repeated headers, and other clearly excluded material as a material validation error that requires correction.
as.sfi_has_child_instructions:
Resolve Ghana Mathematics Basic 4-6 hasChild relationships conservatively. Use finalized SFIs only, and choose the direct parent only from the supplied parent_candidates. The expected source hierarchy is StandardsFramework -> Grade -> Strand -> Sub-Strand -> Content Standard -> Indicator when those source-visible grouping SFIs exist.

Use the Ghana source organization as primary evidence: the document organizes content standards by grade level; within each grade, content is grouped by strands; each strand is subdivided into sub-strands; content standards group related indicators; indicators are learning outcomes. Therefore:
- Grade SFIs such as BASIC 4, BASIC 5, and BASIC 6 should normally attach directly to the StandardsFramework root.
- Strand SFIs should attach to the correct Grade, not to another grade with the same strand label.
- Sub-Strand SFIs should attach to the correct Strand within the correct Grade/source context.
- Content Standard SFIs should attach to the most specific matching Sub-Strand. Do not attach a Content Standard directly to a Strand or Grade unless the direct parent policy is intentionally expanded later. If no supplied Sub-Strand parent is source-supported, mark the child unresolved rather than selecting a broader non-direct parent.
- Indicator SFIs should attach to the matching Content Standard when its normalized code is the indicator code with the final dot component removed, and source context is compatible. If no supplied Content Standard parent is source-supported, mark the child unresolved rather than selecting a Sub-Strand, Strand, or Grade as a non-direct parent.

Treat code-parent hints as strong evidence only when they map to finalized SFI endpoints with compatible source context. Do not choose parents by code alone when source evidence conflicts, when codes are malformed, or when same-code/different-content audit flags are present. Repeated labels such as Strand 1, Sub-strand 1, Number, Data, Measurement, or Fractions are not globally unique; use grade, source order, source segment/window, table context, and section-path evidence to choose the correct scoped parent. Select the StandardsFramework root only for top-level Grade items or when no source-supported finalized SFI parent is available. Choose exactly one direct parent per child unless unresolved.

For coded children, use the code as scope evidence when the code structure is hierarchical. A coded child should not be attached to a sibling grouping whose ordinal, level, topic, strand, domain, cluster, or other source-scope position conflicts with the child code. If a candidate parent has the expected immediate parent statement type but its scope conflicts with the child code, do not select it merely because it is nearby, active in the outline stack, or appears in stale section-path evidence.

When the exact immediate parent implied by a coded child is available in parent_candidates, prefer that parent unless source-local evidence clearly contradicts the code. Strong supporting evidence includes code-parent hints, active_outline_stack_parent, same source segment/window/table, and the most recent/local section-path labels.

When the exact immediate parent implied by a coded child is not available, do not fall back to a sibling parent of the same immediate-parent type or a broader non-direct ancestor unless the explicit parent-type policy is intentionally expanded later. Use unresolved=true so the pipeline emits an auditable StandardsFramework root fallback edge.

Explicit Ghana Basic 4-6 coded-hierarchy precedence rule:
- Ghana Basic 4-6 codes are hierarchical curriculum identifiers. For Content Standards, interpret codes of the form B{grade}.{strand}.{sub_strand}.{content_standard} as grade/strand/sub-strand/content-standard scope evidence; for Indicators, interpret B{grade}.{strand}.{sub_strand}.{content_standard}.{indicator} as grade/strand/sub-strand/content-standard/indicator scope evidence.
- If any coded Content Standard implies an immediate Sub-Strand parent such as B4.1.4, B5.1.2, B5.3.4, or B6.3.1, but no finalized Sub-Strand SFI for that exact grade/strand/sub-strand scope is supplied in parent_candidates, do not attach the child to a visible, nearby, topical, or active Sub-Strand with a different sub-strand ordinal such as B4.1.3, B5.1.1, B5.1.3, B5.3.3, or B6.3.3. Treat the visible section path as incomplete or conflicting rather than as permission to override the coded hierarchy.
- Apply the same rule consistently to all sibling records in the same missing-parent code family, regardless of grade or strand. For example, if B5.1.2.x Content Standards are present but the Basic 5 Number Sub-Strand 2 organizer is missing/omitted from finalized SFIs, all B5.1.2.x Content Standards should be marked unresolved/root fallback unless the exact B5.1.2 Sub-Strand parent is available. Likewise, if B4.1.4.x, B4.1.5.x, B5.1.4.x, B5.1.5.x, B5.3.4.x, or B6.3.1.x Content Standards imply missing exact Sub-Strand parents, do not attach some children to nearby sibling Sub-Strands while leaving others unresolved.
- Active outline stack, section_path labels, nearby source context, and visible body headings may support a parent only when they do not conflict with the coded hierarchy. If they conflict with the code-implied direct parent scope and no exact parent exists, set unresolved=true.

Numeric sub-strand ordinal is controlling for Ghana coded Content Standards:
- Do not reinterpret, waive, or override the numeric sub-strand component of a Ghana Content Standard code because a nearby grouping has a semantically related label. For codes of the form B{grade}.{strand}.{sub_strand}.{content_standard}, the third numeric component is the controlling sub-strand ordinal for parent selection.
- A Content Standard coded B5.1.4.x requires an exact B5.1.4 Sub-Strand parent if one exists in parent_candidates. If no exact B5.1.4 Sub-Strand parent exists, mark unresolved/root fallback. Do not attach it to Sub-Strand 3: Fractions, Sub-Strand 1, or any other semantically related sibling.
- The same rule applies to any coded Content Standard family: B4.1.4.x requires B4.1.4, B4.1.5.x requires B4.1.5, B5.1.5.x requires B5.1.5, B5.3.4.x requires B5.3.4, and B6.3.1.x requires B6.3.1 when those exact parents are supplied. If the exact parent is missing, mark unresolved rather than using a sibling Sub-Strand.
- Do not call an ordinal mismatch a source-labeling artifact unless the source visibly provides an explicit correction equating those ordinals. Topical similarity, section_path labels, active outline stack, or nearby source order are not enough to override the numeric code ordinal.

Visible leading code fallback for null-code children:
- If a child SFI has null normalized_statement_code or null statement_code, but candidate_source_text or source_text visibly begins with a Ghana code-like prefix, use that visible leading prefix as source-visible hierarchy evidence for relationship resolution.
- Treat glued prefixes such as "B5.2.3.1.3Create..." as code-like evidence for parent selection when the prefix matches the Ghana indicator structure and the remaining text is the child statement.
- For such null-code Indicators, prefer the finalized Content Standard whose code equals the visible leading indicator code with the final dot component removed, when that parent exists in parent_candidates.
- Do not select a different same-row Content Standard solely because the table row/context includes a noisy parallel-column collision. Same-row evidence must not override a visible leading child code prefix.
- If the visible leading prefix implies a parent that is not available, mark unresolved rather than selecting a conflicting same-row parent.

Treat active_outline_stack_parent as strong retrieval evidence, but not as automatic truth. If the active outline parent is a sibling grouping that conflicts with the child code or most local source scope, choose the code-compatible parent or a broader compatible fallback instead.

Parallel-column and noisy table-row collision policy:
- Choose exactly one direct parent per child unless the child is unresolved. Do not emit multiple hasChild parents for the same SFI.
- Ghana source tables can contain noisy parallel-column extraction collisions where a Content Standard cell from one code family appears in the same extracted row or window as an Indicator from another code family. Same table row/window evidence is not sufficient to override a clear child code hierarchy.
- For an Indicator with a parseable code, its direct parent must be the Content Standard implied by removing the final dot component, when that exact finalized Content Standard is present and source context is compatible. Do not also attach the Indicator to another Content Standard with a different code merely because the other Content Standard appears in the same extracted row, adjacent table cell, or active outline context.
- If table-local evidence points to a different coded Content Standard than the child's code-implied parent, treat that as a table-layout or extraction collision. Prefer the exact code-implied Content Standard when present; if the code-implied parent is absent or the source context is genuinely ambiguous, mark unresolved rather than selecting multiple parents or a conflicting same-row parent.
- If a visible child code prefix and a same-row Content Standard point to different parent codes, the visible child code prefix wins unless the source visibly marks the code prefix as erroneous. The same-row Content Standard is treated as a table extraction/layout collision, not as parent evidence.

Same-code and table-continuation disambiguation for Ghana curriculum tables:
- Some Ghana tables repeat or reuse a content-standard code for materially different source-visible content standards. In these same-code/different-content cases, choose the parent supported by the child indicator's actual source table row/span and local table context, not the parent whose description merely seems more semantically related to the indicator topic.
- The left CONTENT STANDARDS column can continue a content standard across multiple indicator rows/pages with visible CONT'D text or row-span behavior. When an indicator is on a row governed by such a continued content standard, attach it to that exact finalized content standard if it is available in parent_candidates, even if another finalized content standard has the same normalized code.
- For duplicate-code parent candidates, same source_context_key, same table context, same source segment/window, and active local outline/continued-row evidence should outweigh topical similarity. Do not select a same-code sibling because it sounds like a better conceptual match when the table row or continued source context points to another parent.
- If the source table context clearly identifies one same-code parent but code-parent hints alone cannot distinguish between same-code candidates, treat table-local evidence as decisive. Use broader fallback only when the source-local parent is not available in parent_candidates.
